bias: 'A potential major swing low, the final trapdoor, and the prospect of a failed lower distribution.' Sellers remain firmly in control — Tuesday liquidated NQ through the Nov 5 RTH spike low (26718-26732) to 26658.5 before buyers responded aggressively and reclaimed it; ES fell to 7308 and value shifted sharply lower in both — but ES is nearing completion of the longstanding trapdoor setup (7230s-7240s) while NQ/QQQ approach backtests of their prior all-time highs (NQ proxy 26366.5; a full QQQ backtest of 637.01 implies NQ ~26261, inside 26258-26291). His 'nearly perfect' swing-low scenario: ES into the 7230s-40s, ideally a quick sweep below, while NQ/QQQ complete fresh backtests — 'if that scenario develops, I intend to take a meaningful shot on the long side.' Not calling a bottom: 'I'm identifying the conditions under which I would be particularly interested in buying one.' Both initially rallied on NVDA earnings and gave most of it back; a promising rally that lets one final seller exit, producing one last liquidation into the references, is his ideal. The mirror image of last week's failed upper distribution is now possible: a sustained reclaim of the higher distribution that leaves Tuesday's lower distribution behind would be a meaningful change.
wildcard: Globex reopen (18:00-18:35 ET, after the letter): NQ ran to 27605 — into 27588-27622 — and ES to 7434.75, right at Tuesday's high; the 'promising rally' is already in progress overnight, so the gap-higher setups (es1/es2, nq1/nq2) are the live ones at the open and he evaluates each session with fresh eyes. Post-NVDA: setups kept general — the overnight auction could materially alter the open, so let developing price action dictate execution (nothing graded). QQQ nearly perfectly defended its Nov 5 close/low Tuesday; he'll give QQQ room to ~633-634 but won't initiate longs on continued weakness below that. 'At every major swing low, price is objectively bearish' — a sustained break of Tuesday's low is objectively a continuation short, while he actively looks for a reason to get long at the major references. The indices are near a point where they either establish a meaningful low (here or via the final liquidation) or the larger technical picture deteriorates considerably.
